items.name: GATE_LIMITS
items.doc: The legal range of each gate field (engineering units). The widget clamps drags to these, `normalizeGate` enforces them, the row's codec refuses by them and the travel sheet publishes them — one source of truth. `rangeDb` reaches GATE_RANGE_FLOOR_DB, shown as "−∞" in readouts (a gate fully closed is silence).

items.name: GATE_KEY_SOURCES
items.doc: Where the gate listens: its own input (self), or the key it is handed (sidechain), in the order of the integer the key port carries.

items.name: GATE_KEY_LIMITS

source.origin: the console engine's keyed gate detector filter travels: hpHz and lpHz, 0 (off) to 20000 Hz in whole Hz, no come-up value (the /channel/{kind}/{index}/gate/key row)

items.doc: The travel of each edge of the keyed gate's detector filter, 0 (off) up to 20 kHz in whole Hz, as the console's `/channel/{kind}/{index}/gate/key` row serves them (the console's GATE_KEY_LIMITS). A property of the detector filter, not of any desk: no come-up value is declared.

items.name: GATE_KEY_LISTENS

source.origin: first declared in omx-dsp data/kernels/gate.json at 5d7e9c614694, shipped in omx-dsp 0.27.0; implemented at include/omxdsp/fx/omx_gate_instance.h#listen_on

items.doc: While on, the outputs carry what the gate's detector reads: the key (the sidechain, or the gate's own mono sum) after the key filter and the tilt on both outputs, or, for a self-keyed gate with no key filter and a flat tilt, each input leg on its own output, since the detector then reads the legs. The gate keeps running underneath. It comes up off.

items.name: GATE_KEY_TILT_DB_RANGE

source.origin: first declared in omx-dsp data/kernels/gate.json at 5d7e9c614694, shipped in omx-dsp 0.27.0; implemented at include/omxdsp/fx/omx_gate_instance.h#tilt_slope

items.doc: The key's tilt, in dB per octave at KEY_TILT_PIVOT_HZ, after the key filter: positive lets the gate open on a brighter key (a tom, a snare) and stay shut on the low end, negative the other way (omx_tilt, the compressor's key tilt). 0 is flat, the come-up value, bit for bit.
